preamble: The transformation from 'ch' to 't' involves losing the palatal release, leaving only the simple alveolar stop.

examples.note: Common phonological simplification in first-language acquisition; affricate simplified to stop.
Polynesian languages lacking [tʃ] substitute [t] in English loanwords. The specific form 'tati' could not be verified; flagged as unconfirmed.

sources: Smith, N. V. (1973). The Acquisition of Phonology: A Case Study. Cambridge University Press. TalkBank. https://talkbank.org/phon/access/Eng-UK/0docs/smith1973.pdf
